units.text: MK-1: an exactly simulated two-qubit ZZ-feature-map fidelity kernel,\\ with machine-checked kernel properties\\ and a finite-shot hardware check

MK-1 is a small, self-contained implementation of a quantum fidelity kernel on two qubits: a ZZ-type feature map $U(x)$, the compute--uncompute estimator $K(x,x')=|\langle 00|U(x')^\dagger U(x)|00\rangle|^2$, and a visualisation of the kernel-SVM pipeline.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: The construction is not new; it follows Havl\'{\i}\v{c}ek et al.~\cite{havlicek} and Schuld--Killoran~\cite{schuld}.

This note records exactly what the code computes, documents a defect in the original script (its ``entangling'' gate was a no-op, so the state is a product state and the kernel factorises, proved in Lean on explicit $4\times4$ matrices), and lists what is machine-checked in Lean~4 with Mathlib: for any unitary feature map, $K(x,x)=1$, symmetry, $0\le K\le 1$, compute--uncompute equals state fidelity, and positive semidefiniteness of the Gram matrix.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: A small finite-shot study (6 circuits, $N=256$--$8192$) on a simulator and on one IBM device is reported.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: No quantum advantage or new learning-theoretic claim is made, and no SVM is trained.
The construction
Qubit 0 is the first tensor factor and the CNOT control.

For $x=(x_0,x_1)\in\mathbb{R}^2$, \[ U(x)=\mathrm{CNOT}\,(I\otimes R_Z(2x_0x_1))\,\mathrm{CNOT}\,(R_Z(2x_0)\otimes R_Z(2x_1))\,(H\otimes H), \qquad R_Z(\theta)=\mathrm{diag}(e^{-i\theta/2},e^{i\theta/2}).
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: \] Since $\mathrm{CNOT}(I\otimes R_Z(\theta))\mathrm{CNOT}=e^{-i\theta Z\otimes Z/2}$, writing basis states by signs $s\in\{\pm1\}^2$, \[ U(x)|00\rangle=\tfrac12\sum_{s} e^{-i\varphi(s,x)}|s\rangle,\qquad \varphi(s,x)=x_0s_0+x_1s_1+x_0x_1s_0s_1, \] so with $\Delta=x-x'$ and $\Delta_{01}=x_0x_1-x_0'x_1'$, \[ K(x,x')=\Bigl|\tfrac14\sum_{s}e^{-i(\Delta_0s_0+\Delta_1s_1+\Delta_{01}s_0s_1)}\Bigr|^2 .
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: \[ U(x)|00\rangle=\tfrac12\sum_{s} e^{-i\varphi(s,x)}|s\rangle,\qquad \varphi(s,x)=x_0s_0+x_1s_1+x_0x_1s_0s_1, \]
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: \] This is one layer of the ZZ feature map of~\cite{havlicek} with the simplified pair coefficient $x_0x_1$ (their map uses $(\pi-x_0)(\pi-x_1)$ and two layers).
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: With one layer, and on two qubits, the kernel has the closed form above and is trivially classically computable; MK-1 is a teaching and testing artefact.
The closed form (\texttt{kernel\_closed\_form}) agrees with the statevector kernel to $10^{-12}$ in the tests ($1.3\times10^{-15}$ on the 16 pairs of Section~\ref{sec:shots}).
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: General results on when quantum kernels concentrate or can be dequantised~\cite{kubler,thanasilp,huang} are cited, not proved or formalised here.
A defect in the original script
The original \texttt{mk1\_moving\_tower.py} (kept in \texttt{original/}) applied the middle $R_Z(2x_0x_1)$ to the \emph{control} qubit.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: A diagonal gate on the control commutes with CNOT, so the two CNOTs cancel and no $Z\otimes Z$ phase is produced; the kernel becomes the product $\cos^2(\Delta_0+\Delta_{01})\cos^2\Delta_1$.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: The package keeps this as \texttt{variant="legacy"} for reproducibility and uses the corrected map by default.

Both facts ($\mathrm{CNOT}(D\otimes I)\mathrm{CNOT}=D\otimes I$ and the $Z\otimes Z$ phase for a target gate) are proved in Lean (\texttt{cnot\_onControl\_cnot}\lean{MK1.cnot_onControl_cnot}, also stated as \texttt{phantom\_entangler}\lean{MK1.phantom_entangler}; \texttt{cnot\_onTarget\_cnot}\lean{MK1.cnot_onTarget_cnot}).
notes: MK1.cnot_onControl_cnot [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
MK1.phantom_entangler [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
MK1.cnot_onTarget_cnot [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound

units.text: \texttt{lean/MK1/Factorization.lean} proves on explicit $4\times4$ complex matrices that the legacy state is a product state (\texttt{legacyState\_eq\_prod}\lean{MK1.legacyState_eq_prod}), that inner products and kernels of product states factor (\texttt{inner\_prod2}\lean{MK1.inner_prod2}, \texttt{kernel4\_prod2}\lean{MK1.kernel4_prod2}), hence the legacy kernel is a product of single-qubit kernels (\texttt{legacy\_kernel\_factors}\lean{MK1.legacy_kernel_factors}); it also proves \texttt{kernel4\_symm}\lean{MK1.kernel4_symm} and \texttt{kernel4\_self}\lean{MK1.kernel4_self} for the concrete $4$-dimensional kernel.

units.text: What is machine-checked
\texttt{lean/MK1/FidelityKernel.lean} defines $K_\psi(x,y)=|\langle\psi(y),\psi(x)\rangle|^2$ for any family $\psi$ in a complex inner product space and proves:
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: \texttt{fidelity\_self}\lean{MK1.fidelity_self}, \texttt{fidelity\_symm}\lean{MK1.fidelity_symm}, \texttt{fidelity\_nonneg}\lean{MK1.fidelity_nonneg}, \texttt{fidelity\_le\_one}\lean{MK1.fidelity_le_one}: $K(x,x)=1$ for unit states, symmetry, $0\le K\le1$ (Cauchy--Schwarz);
notes: MK1.fidelity_self [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
MK1.fidelity_symm [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
MK1.fidelity_nonneg [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
MK1.fidelity_le_one [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound

units.text: \texttt{norm\_featureState}\lean{MK1.norm_featureState}, \texttt{computeUncompute\_eq\_fidelity}\lean{MK1.computeUncompute_eq_fidelity}: states $U(x)v$ from unitaries (linear isometry equivalences) are unit vectors, and $|\langle v,U(y)^{-1}U(x)v\rangle|^2=K(x,y)$;
notes: MK1.norm_featureState [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound
MK1.computeUncompute_eq_fidelity [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound

units.text: \texttt{fidelity\_gram\_posSemidef}\lean{MK1.fidelity_gram_posSemidef}: for states in $\mathbb{C}^n$ and finitely many points, the matrix $[K(x_j,x_i)]$ is positive semidefinite, via $|\langle a,b\rangle|^2=\langle a\otimes\bar a,b\otimes\bar b\rangle$ and Mathlib's Gram-matrix theorem.
notes: MK1.fidelity_gram_posSemidef [theorem] axioms: propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound

units.text: All are \texttt{sorry}-free; \texttt{AxiomAudit.lean} shows only \texttt{propext}, \texttt{Classical.choice}, \texttt{Quot.sound}; CI rebuilds and audits on every push.
These are standard facts; the Lean development checks them, it does not establish anything new.

The Lean code does not model the specific gate angles beyond the CNOT identities and the legacy factorisation; the agreement of the numerical circuit with the closed form is checked by the Python tests.
What is tested numerically

The Python tests (CI, every push) check for both variants: unitarity of $U(x)$; $K(x,x)=1$; symmetry; $0\le K\le1$; compute--uncompute equals $|\langle\psi(x')|\psi(x)\rangle|^2$; agreement with the matrix-free closed form to $10^{-12}$; Gram matrices symmetric with minimum eigenvalue $>-10^{-10}$; and the two CNOT identities.
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: Finite-shot estimation
\label{sec:shots} For four points (seed 7) the exact Gram matrix has off-diagonal entries $0.1246, 0.0840, 0.2525, 0.9176, 0.3283, 0.3298$ (minimum eigenvalue $0.081$).
notes: mathematical content with no Lean mapping

units.text: Each is estimated as the frequency of $00$ in a compute--uncompute circuit, using the first $N$ of 8192 shots.

Limitations
Two qubits; one hardware job without mitigation; no SVM is trained in the package (the DUAL/DECIDE stages are illustrative); no claim of quantum advantage.
For the limits of such kernels see~\cite{kubler}.
